public_rationale: The NeurIPS audit identifies a substantial collection of 2025 publications with human-verified fabricated or corrupted references that survived review. That meets the ordinary reading that lots of defective AI-linked material would enter the literature. The support is for defective content in many papers, not for a claim that those papers were wholly generated or scientifically worthless.
limitations: The decisive audit concerns conference proceedings; journal evidence is corroborative.
GPTZero sells detection tools and has a commercial interest in the problem.
AI attribution remains inferential, and the audit has a small inconsistency in its paper count.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Many bad LLM-generated papers will get through review into the scientific literature.

statement.excerpt: Lots of bad stuff is going to sneak in.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that numerous papers containing defective LLM-generated material will pass review and enter the scientific literature.
Fabricated references count as defective material even when a paper's main findings remain valid.
Lots means a documented collection of many distinct papers, rather than isolated anecdotes; it does not require a majority of published research.
Peer-reviewed scientific conference proceedings are included alongside journals.
Only publications after the post can settle this forecast.
criteria.support_condition: A reproducible audit documents numerous post-March-15-2024 peer-reviewed publications containing verified fabricated references or other substantive defects credibly linked to LLM use.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A representative audit over an agreed forecast period shows that suspected cases are false positives or that defective LLM-generated material is consistently caught before publication.

evidence.locator: Opening paragraph and following table of NeurIPS papers
evidence.explanation: The investigation lists fabricated or corrupted references in dozens of accepted, presented NeurIPS 2025 papers and reports human verification. This establishes numerous defective publications after the forecast, although attribution to AI is inferred from the error patterns and text analysis.

evidence.locator: Printed page 8, Systemic responses and failure modes
evidence.explanation: The study reports that 85.3% of the examined citation defects persisted into journal publications. This corroborates the failure mode, but its linked-paper sample spans multiple years and unmatched references are not individually proven LLM outputs, so it is not the decisive post-forecast count.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: Dozens of distinct papers published through NeurIPS 2025 contained verified citation defects characteristic of LLM generation after passing review; the audit documenting them was public before the evaluation date.
